content.value: The Elixir/Phoenix application in `api/` — the server every other surface talks to.
The Phoenix API is the heart of Barkpark: an Elixir/Phoenix app living in

that serves HTTP API v1, renders LiveView Studio, runs background jobs, and owns every plugin. While it is listed among the Surfaces as the server-side client surface, it is really the hub the Go TUI, bp CLI, and JS SDK all orbit.
Over HTTP API v1 it exposes Document reads, Mutation writes validated against Schema v2, Search queries, and the Capabilities Manifest at
that lets clients self-discover. Authentication runs through Auth and Tokens. After a write it fans out Webhooks for Cache Revalidation downstream.

The same app hosts LiveView Studio, the server-rendered editing UI, including the Graph View pane. Long-running and deferred work — Edge Extractor runs, search indexing, Migration tasks — execute on the Oban Worker queue rather than blocking request handlers.

Every Plugins surface — OnixEdit, Bulldocs, Tasks Plugin, Media Plugin, Frt Plugin — rides the Plugin Behaviour inside this app. The Fresh Install Invariant guarantees that with all of them switched off, the Phoenix API still serves content correctly. Running it in the real world — deploy discipline, the systemd Service, background queues — is the domain of Operations; in Production it runs as a systemd Service behind Caddy on the Hetzner origin.
